### Printing in the UK industry analysis

The popularity of digital alternatives to printed materials has been holding the Printing industry back in recent years. Demand for printed materials has fallen as consumers and businesses have gradually transitioned towards online trading. Demand has also been edging downwards due to the growing popularity of reading online and through other electronic alternatives (e.g. e-readers and smartphones). Revenue is anticipated to tumble at a compound annual rate of 4.1% over the five years through 2024-25 to £9.2 billion, while profit is set to inch up to 5.5% as printing companies get some respite from pressures like inflation and high utility costs.

#### Trends and Insights

- Pricing determines a printers’ competitiveness. High fragmentation in the market means clients have plenty of potential printers to choose from, so it goes without saying that they’ll usually choose the printer that gives them more for their money.
- Proximity to the capital is a big draw for printing companies. London offers easy access to lots of potential customers, keeping sales flowing. That’s why the South East and London contain the most establishments.
- Book printing remains the biggest source of revenue. This is despite soaring competition from digital alternatives, like e-books and audiobooks, eating into printed book production.
- Sales to major markets tumble. Printing companies are struggling to cope with the quick decline in magazine and newspaper circulation numbers, which is slashing demand for printing services.

## Industry Statistics and Trends

### Market size and recent performance (2015-2030)

Industry revenue has declined at a CAGR of 4.1 % over the past five years, to reach an estimated £9.2bn in 2025.

#### Trends and Insights

#### Printers grapple with falling newspaper and magazine circulation numbers

- Additional trends and insights available with purchase
- The transition to online news sources has resulted in a drastic decline in the sale of some printed goods, like newspapers and magazines. This was exacerbated in 2020-21, when the COVID-19 pandemic hit newspaper printing hard. Data from the Audit Bureau of Circulations (ABC) reveals that newspaper circulation numbers continue to sink in 2024-25, with most newspapers seeing a double-digit year-on-year drop in January 2025. For example, regional newspaper circulation dropped by a 16% average in 2024, while major national publications like The Daily Mail and the Financial Times tumbled by 7% and 5%, respectively, according to the ABC. This is hitting UK printing companies specialised in newspaper and magazine printing.

#### High fashion advertisements could offer hope for magazine printers in the UK

- According to Business of Fashion, printed magazines are brands’ new favourite marketing tactic in 2024-25. Brands from Madhappy and Patta to Bottega Veneta are embracing print magazines full of on-brand editorial content as they attempt to escape online algorithms and bypass the drawbacks of social media marketing.

Trade advertising material and catalogues is the largest segment of the Printing in the UK.

#### Trends and Insights

Book printing remains steady despite intense competition

- More insights available in the full report
- The UK book publishing industry is robust, having consistently grown over the past few years despite massive macroeconomic headwinds, including reduced consumer spending and inflated costs. According to the Publishers Association (PA), UK publishing income increased by 3% in 2023 following a 4% hike in 2022, both marketing record-breaking years as publishing revenue surpassed £7 billion for the first time in 2023, supporting demand for book printing services.

## About this industry

#### Industry definition

Companies in this industry print books, magazines, annual reports, brochures, labels, tags, posters, diaries, calendars, maps, stamps, postcards and greeting cards, security papers, cheques, banknotes and other products. The industry also includes the printing of newspapers and periodicals that appear less than four times a week.

#### What's included in this industry?

Products and services covered in the Printing industry in the United Kingdom include Trade advertising material and catalogues , Books, brochures and leaflets , Newspapers, magazines, journals and periodicals, Security printing, Printing on non-paper materials, Paper packaging, inserts and tickets and Maps and atlases.

#### Companies

Companies covered in the Printing industry in the United Kingdom include Walstead Group Ltd, DS Smith Ltd and Clays Ltd.
